disposition_reason: Original ICP-MS concentrations of Al, Se, Zn, Cd, Cu and Pb in raw and pasteurized milk, white and yellow cheese and yoghurt bought in three regions of Alexandria.

unresolved: Table 2 overall means (Pb 3.541, Cd 0.212, Al 1.211, Cu 1.532, Zn 6.965, Se 0.151 ppm = µg/mL) are pooled across products; not extracted as findings; the Se pooled mean (0.151) exceeds every Se maximum in Table 1.

Many Table 1 cells repeat identical mean ± SD across regions (e.g., Zn in white cheese 10.75 ± 6.749 in Eastern and Central, Cd and Cu yellow cheese values nearly identical), which suggests copying in the table.
Number of samples per product per region is not clear: the methods say 30 random samples of raw milk and four other dairy products; Table 1 says n = 30 for each sampling site.
No LOD, LOQ, certified reference material or recovery data are reported; lead means of 1.8-4.4 mg/kg in milk are far above typical published milk values.
The Discussion states "Pb and Cd ... (7.421, and 5.013 ppm)", but 5.013 is the copper maximum, not cadmium.
